rv.q: So, as in the case with playwright/performer Keith Hamilton Cobb's breathtaking theatrical exploration, American Moor, when an African-American actor approaches the character of Othello, he brings with him a more personal understanding of the man's situation...
“American Moor” is the first, so far this year, to give an actor like Cobb his due.
Keith Hamilton Cobb delivers a compelling turn in this deeply felt meditation on Shakespeare and racism.

Believe you me, he indisputable impresses onlookers that he’s got the goods for whatever he’s about to do, certainly as directed by Kim Weild. And when it becomes clear the actor he’s embodying is aiming to land the title role, he looks to have a damn good chance.

cn.t: Keith Hamilton Cobb's solo show transforms an Othello audition into a powerful meditation on race and theater. Critics praise the emotionally charged, fiery performance piece, though its 90-minute format divides some.
